stop_status: NO CONFIRMED MEMORY-SAFETY DEFECT REMAINS IN THE REVIEWED SCOPE. One genuine out-of-bounds read existed in the resumption binder path (tls13_psk_do_binder read hashsize bytes through a bare *const u8 supplied from an attacker-length binder) and is fixed. The boundary is OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED: residuals are enumerated below and BOUNDARY/SEAL evidence was not run.

boundaries.operation: ClientHello extension collection and body parsing
boundaries.before: One in-place walk over the raw block wrote s->ext_hostname, s->s3.alpn_proposed, s->ext_status_type, s->post_handshake_auth and s->s3.tmp.peer_sigalgs as each extension was reached; a later malformed extension left those members published on a rejected hello. Lengths were computed by hand (eb[i], 5+nlen, 2+list_len, min(...)) and several truncations silently stopped the walk.
boundaries.after: A two-pass safe function over &[u8]: pass 1 replays tls_collect_extensions (header framing, duplicate recognised type, pre_shared_key last); pass 2 parses each body through SliceCursor into ParsedExtensions, which only borrows the handshake message. The function returns Result<ParsedExtensions, HelloReject> and never touches Ssl.
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED: mid-walk publication; unchecked/manual length arithmetic; silent truncation acceptance.

boundaries.operation: publication of the parsed extension set into the connection
boundaries.before: No single commit point; five members were written at five different points in the walk.
boundaries.after: One unsafe fn with five unsafe blocks is the only writer: it allocates the SNI C-string and ALPN blob first (OwnedCStr/OwnedBuf, so a failure releases them), stores sigalgs next, copies client_random/session-id, then installs SNI, ALPN, status type and PHA. It runs only after the whole block and the client_hello callback succeed.
boundaries.mechanism: RELOCATED: five publication unsafe blocks into one auditable function; behaviourally atomic on rejected hellos.

boundaries.before: About a dozen framing/extension failures returned 0 with no alert and no MSG_FLOW_ERROR transition; the caller supplied a generic internal error only when reached through the driver.
boundaries.after: Every failure returns through one closure that calls ossl_statem_fatal with the authority's alert/reason, which sets MSG_FLOW_ERROR and writes the fatal alert. A rejected ClientHello is therefore explicitly poisoned, never reusable with partial state (the authority also terminates on every one of these paths).
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED: silent 0 returns. RELOCATED: one unsafe call site for the fatal transition.

boundaries.before: received was *const u8; the function read md_size bytes unconditionally. tls_process_client_hello passed psk_binder.as_ptr() for a binder of any non-zero length. A client with a valid ticket and a 1-byte binder caused an out-of-bounds read past the ClientHello message.
boundaries.after: received is &[u8]; the function requires received.len() == hashsize before the full-length constant-time accumulation. The caller also computes the session cipher's digest size and refuses a resolved-ticket binder whose length differs with the authority's DECODE_ERROR/BAD_EXTENSION, and bounds the binder transcript offset against hs.len().
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED: a received-binder length the input does not contain (the only unsafe deref in the compare now reads the caller's hashsize buffer, with the slice length checked).
boundaries.state: FIXED (author) + regression test binder_length_must_match_the_digest_size. Independent review NOT_RUN.

unsafe_ops.retained: 51 blocks in tls_process_client_hello (the pre-existing connection/driver calls and the one fatal-transition closure) + 5 in commit_client_hello. t1_lib.rs's block count is unchanged (validation moved to the safe helper). tls13_enc.rs's block count is unchanged but the compare now dereferences only the writable output buffer.
unsafe_ops.introduced: 5 blocks, all in commit_client_hello: two allocation calls (OwnedCStr::strndup, OwnedBuf::new_memdup), one sigalgs store, one member-slot clear/store pair, and the client_random/tmp_session_id copies. Each has a SAFETY contract naming the live connection and the member-buffer/allocator invariant.

malformed_cases.note: Authority behaviour: tls_parse_ctos_psk returns 1 at `if (sess == NULL) return 1;` before reading the binders vector (extensions_srvr.c:1439-1453). The binder count is only checked once a ticket resolves; this no-ticket harness cannot reach that branch, so acceptance is the authority's documented outcome, not a missed rejection. A resolved-ticket binder of the wrong length is now fatal DECODE_ERROR/BAD_EXTENSION (same file, resumption arm).

state_preservation.authority: Every listed parse failure calls SSLfatal, whose ossl_statem_send_fatal sets MSG_FLOW_ERROR and sends the fatal alert; the connection is terminated (ssl/statem/statem.c:147-174). OpenSSL does not retry a ClientHello on the same SSL object after a fatal parse error.
state_preservation.observed: assert_rejected checks ossl_statem_in_error(s) != 0 for every malformed case. rejected_hello_publishes_no_extension_state additionally proves no extension-derived member was published before the failure: ext_hostname NULL, s3_alpn_proposed (NULL,0), post_handshake_auth 0, ext_status_type TLSEXT_STATUSTYPE_NOTHING, tmp_session_id_len 0, client_random all-zero.

The real parser on the same malformed input is asserted clean by rejected_hello_publishes_no_extension_state.

compatibility_corrections: Duplicate recognised extensions: was accepted; now SSL_AD_ILLEGAL_PARAMETER / SSL_R_BAD_EXTENSION (extensions.c tls_collect_extensions).

Truncated/over-long extension vector, trailing bytes after it, and an over-long compression vector: were silently treated as no/partial extensions; now SSL_AD_DECODE_ERROR / SSL_R_LENGTH_MISMATCH (statem_srvr.c:1621-1658).
supported_versions overrun or half version: was clamped; now SSL_AD_PROTOCOL_VERSION / SSL_R_LENGTH_MISMATCH. Empty list: SSL_AD_PROTOCOL_VERSION / SSL_R_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL.
zero-length or odd-length supported_groups: was accepted; now SSL_AD_DECODE_ERROR / SSL_R_BAD_EXTENSION.
truncated key_share entry: was silently dropped; now SSL_AD_DECODE_ERROR / SSL_R_LENGTH_MISMATCH.
empty/over-long psk_key_exchange_modes: was ignored; now SSL_AD_DECODE_ERROR / SSL_R_BAD_EXTENSION.
truncated PSK identity entry: was silently ignored; now SSL_AD_DECODE_ERROR / SSL_R_BAD_EXTENSION.
pre_shared_key without psk_key_exchange_modes: was accepted; now TLS13_AD_MISSING_EXTENSION / SSL_R_MISSING_PSK_KEX_MODES_EXTENSION (extensions.c final_psk).
non-empty post_handshake_auth: reason was SSL_R_BAD_EXTENSION; now SSL_R_POST_HANDSHAKE_AUTH_ENCODING_ERR.

All of the above move the reduced reader toward the pinned authority; none is a divergence from OpenSSL. Multi-fault hellos can still report a different first error than the authority because body parsers run in wire order rather than ext_defs order (residual).

discharged: No safe caller can construct a &[u8] over the extension input longer than the message: parse_client_hello_extensions is safe, uses only SliceCursor, and returns slices that lie inside exts.
A rejected ClientHello cannot publish a partial extension set: the parse has no connection access and the commit runs only after full success.
Every rejection raises the authority's alert/reason and enters MSG_FLOW_ERROR.
A received TLS1.3 binder shorter/longer than the digest size can no longer be read out of bounds.
retained: commit_client_hello is unsafe and requires s live, random exactly 32 bytes, session_id <= 32 bytes, and parsed borrowing a live message; the sole caller establishes all four.
The five retained unsafe blocks in the parse function rely on the caller's `s` liveness contract (unchanged from before).
introduced: commit_client_hello's allocation-then-install order: an allocation failure leaves the previous member values in place and the state machine poisoned; callers must not resume the connection after Err.
tls13_psk_do_binder now requires received.len() == hashsize; a caller that cannot establish it gets 0 (no compare) rather than UB.

residuals.finding: Custom extensions (SSL_CTX_add_custom_ext) are not modelled, so a duplicate custom extension type is not detected.
Context-inappropriate extension rejection (extensions.c verify_extension) is not modelled, e.g. use_srtp in a TLS ClientHello is ignored rather than ILLEGAL_PARAMETER/BAD_EXTENSION.

status_request validates framing only; responder-id DER and request-extension DER are not parsed (pre-existing reduction). The reduced reader also requires the request-extensions vector to end the body where the authority ignores trailing bytes.
SSL_R_MISSING_SUPPORTED_GROUPS_EXTENSION is not enforced (pre-existing module-header boundary).

key_share group membership/priority selection and the HelloRetryRequest path are reduced: the first structurally valid X25519 share is kept; authority group-priority and s3.group_id_candidate/HRR are not modelled.
psk_ke / SSL_OP_ALLOW_NO_DHE_KEX is not modelled; only psk_dhe_ke is honoured.
Body parsers run in wire order, not the authority's ext_defs order, so a hello with several independent faults can report a different first error.
supported_groups keeps at most 32 entries (pre-existing selection buffer).
residuals.disposition: documented; a matching group beyond entry 32 is not selected.
